newsitem.title: Sri lanka: Sri Lanka says to tighten noose on murder suspects.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says to tighten noose on murder suspects.

text.p: Sri Lanka said on Thursday it plans to speed up murder trials, stop granting bail to suspects in murder cases and crack down on unlicensed gun users following the killing of a ruling coalition lawmaker last week.

"The government has already embarked on a series of initiatives to deal with the large number of unlicenced firearms available in the country and the large number of persons who are able to use these firearms," Justice Minister Gamini Lakshman Peiris told reporters.

Politicians and political activists in Sri Lanka own a large number of guns, some of them unlicensed, to guard themselves against possible attack by Tamil rebels who are fighting a separatist war in the country's north and east.
The murder of Nalanda Ellawala in the southern town of Ratnapura has highlighted more than ever the need to tighten the law to bring gun-carrying political activists to justice, Peiris said.
Shortly after he spoke, the key suspect in the lawmaker's killing, which sparked two days of riots in Ratnaura, turned himself in to a Colombo judge after hiding from police for nine days.
Police and court officials said Susantha Punchinilame, a main opposition United National Party (UNP) lawmaker, surrendered to the Colombo Fort area magistrate on Thursday.
They said Punchinilame was remanded prior to being presented before the magistrate of Ratnapura, 80 km (50 miles) from Colombo. Police did not say when Punchinilame would be presented in court.

Fifteen other suspects are already in custody for the killing of the ruling People's Alliance's Ellawala, who was gunned down during a roadside quarrel between supporters of the alliance and those of the rival UNP, Peiris said.
He said the government was also considering appointing new magistrates to shorten the time taken for cases to be heard in lower courts.
A new law will be presented to parliament shortly which will enable courts to deny bail to those accused of using firearms without proper licences and of murder, he said.
Peiris said Punchinilame was out on bail at the time of Ellawala's murder in a pending case over the 1988 killing of three people, including a university student.
